Model registry

Every model is versioned and tracked.

We never run an unregistered model. Every version is pinned, every promotion is justified, and every retirement is recorded.

Our models

HazardPulse uses four prediction models, each specialized for a different type of hazard:

Earthquake model

Combines where large quakes happen in the long run with how they cluster after recent ones. On 2023–2025, scored once, it ranked a cell that went on to have an M6+ quake above one that did not 97% of the time across the globe, and 77% among cells with recent quakes, the harder question.

Hurricane model

For storms the National Hurricane Center tracks, we serve NOAA’s own DTOPS guidance: in a pre-registered test on the 2025 season it beat every alternative, including our own model, ranking a forecast cycle that went on to intensify rapidly above one that did not 93% of the time.

Tornado model (storm-level)

Scores every thunderstorm NOAA tracks for the chance it produces a tornado in the next hour. On every storm of 2025, scored once, it ranked a storm that went on to produce a tornado above one that did not 97% of the time.

Tornado model (day-ahead)

Uses weather parameters to predict tornado environments 12-24 hours ahead. It ranks a tornado environment above a non-tornado one 64% of the time (AUC 0.644; this is a hard problem).

Models are only promoted after they beat the previous version on holdout data. Models that fail quality checks are rejected.

Promotion policy

Requirements for promotion

  • Statistically significant improvement on holdout set (AUC or Brier)
  • No regression in calibration or false alarm rate
  • Passes all gate checks (G0-G12) on validation corpus
  • Training data cutoff documented and frozen
  • Feature set and architecture documented in registry

Rejection criteria

  • Brier score above calibration floor threshold (0.25)
  • False alarm rate regression exceeding 5%
  • Calibration error exceeding 8% in any bin
  • Inability to produce replay-verified deterministic outputs
  • Missing or incomplete feature documentation
